array.definition: A contiguous, index-addressable block of memory. Element i's address is computed arithmetically from the base, so access is O(1).

hash function.definition: Maps a key to a bucket index, so storing and looking up a value is a direct jump, not a scan.

bucket.definition: One slot of a hash table's backing array, holding the entry (or entries) for keys that hash to it.

collision.definition: When two different keys hash to the same bucket. Resolved with chaining or open addressing.

load factor.definition: A hash table's entries ÷ buckets. Past ~0.7, collisions get frequent and the table resizes and rehashes.

chaining.definition: Each bucket holds a small list; colliding keys are appended to it, so a lookup scans just that short list.

open addressing.definition: Instead of a per-bucket list, probe forward to the next free slot on a collision.

cache.definition: A store of the results of expensive work, so repeat requests are served quickly instead of recomputed.

cache hit.definition: A request whose result is already in the cache, served without redoing the work (a miss must do the work).

eviction policy.definition: The rule a bounded cache uses to decide which entry to drop when full — e.g. LRU.

lru.definition: Least-Recently-Used — an eviction policy that drops the entry left untouched for the longest.

consistent hashing.definition: A scheme that maps keys and nodes onto the same hash ring so that adding or removing a node remaps only about 1/N of the keys, not nearly all of them.

hash ring.definition: The circular hash space (0…2^m, wrapping around) onto which both nodes and keys are hashed; a key is owned by the first node clockwise from its position.

virtual node.definition: Several ring positions per physical node (replicas), used so keys spread evenly across nodes instead of clumping in large gaps.
